## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Adopting an existing setting through the command now prints its progress line twice, so this needs fixing before the adoption records are safe to use.

## Changes
The pull request makes `plan` return an `adopt` entry for each setting that already exists and a trailing `audit` entry with the incoming setting count. It also adds two tests for the audit entry through `run`, plus a new text file, `app/review.txt`.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/planner.py:9 — correctness — Stop `run` from re-emitting adoption progress — `run({"theme": "dark"}, {"theme": "dark"}, emit)` now emits "Adopted theme" twice: once from `plan`'s progress `emit` at `app/planner.py:8`, and again because `app/cli.py:9` renders every non-audit change, including the new `adopt` entry. Before this change, the command printed it once. No test calls `run` with an existing setting. — Users running the command on existing settings see every adoption line twice. — Fix: Skip `adopt` entries in the `app/cli.py:7` filter, the same way `audit` entries are skipped, or stop emitting progress in `plan`. Then add a `run` test that adopts a setting next to `test_command_adds_setting`.
